plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Gnarled, leafless branches burst into fragrant blossoms with a sweet, spicy perfume. They open while frost and even snow are still on the ground. In Japan, ume are loved as the first heralds of spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, typically late January through March, with peak bloom in February in milder parts of Japan
plants.location: Japan, including the Kanto and Kansai regions such as Mito and Kyoto
plants.funFact: Ume blooms weeks before cherry blossoms, and the fruit is pickled into umeboshi, a staple of Japanese cuisine.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Nodding, bell-shaped white flowers with delicate green markings rise on slender stems from the cold earth. They carpet woodlands and gardens in drifts. They are among the first flowers to appear after winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter, generally January to March, with peak bloom often in February
plants.location: Woodlands and gardens across the United Kingdom and western and central Europe
plants.funFact: Snowdrops produce natural antifreeze-like proteins that help them push through frozen soil, and the plant is the original source of the medicine galantamine.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Rounded umbels of trumpet-shaped blue flowers sit on tall, sturdy stems above arching, strap-like leaves. In summer gardens they create a bold, cool-toned display. Bees and butterflies visit them often.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer, roughly December through February or March
plants.location: Coastal gardens in eastern South Africa and across Australia and New Zealand, where it is widely grown
plants.funFact: Despite the common name, it is not a true lily. Its name comes from Greek words meaning love flower.
